issues.body: `attested_review_head` still iterates newest-first but returns only when it encounters `cause == human-arm`, silently skipping a newer authenticated, well-formed record with another cause. With an older `human-arm(head=live)` followed by a newer `injection(head=live)`, it returns the older head and `approval_coverage` can still produce `covers-head`, contrary to the documented `Newest receipt wins` rule. The new matrix does not catch this: the off-cause case has no older human-arm record, while the newest-wins case contains two human-arm records. Historical approval evidence remains reusable across a later park episode.
issues.fix_hint: Select the newest authenticated, well-formed park-reason record first, then return its head only if that newest record has `cause=human-arm`; otherwise return no attestation. Add a literal end-to-end regression with an older matching human-arm receipt followed by a newer authenticated off-cause receipt, asserting that it cannot render `covers-head` and the report cannot exit 0.
issues.title: A newer off-cause park still does not supersede an older human-arm attestation

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 trust-plane defect remains. `attested_review_head` still walks backward until it finds any `human-arm` record, so a newer authenticated off-cause park record does not supersede an older approval attestation. The added tests still separate the off-cause and supersession cases instead of exercising the decisive older-human-arm/newer-off-cause history. A later injection or other park episode can therefore resurrect stale approval evidence and yield `covers-head`. This is materially the same major finding at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
